I been on this land 40 years. My man and me, we do same things every year, what my neighbors do. I don't change much — change is risky, and if the harvest fails, what do we eat?

I got 7.5 mu. I keep 5 mu for the wheat-corn rotation — that's the bread on the table. The other 2.5 mu I put in cotton. Cotton brings cash when the buyer comes, and I been growing it since I was a young bride.

For wheat, I plant in October after the corn comes off. I buy seed from the village store, the kind everybody uses now — not the old seed my mother had. I spread one and a half bags of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — that's the 15-15-15 bag, 50 kg each. So one and a half bag, that comes to about 12 kg of nitrogen from the base. Then come spring when the wheat greens up, I put down half a bag of urea per mu — another 11-12 kg nitrogen. Total nitrogen close to 18 kg per mu, I think. Phosphorus and potash, maybe 7-8 kg each, whatever's in the compound. I water three times — before winter freeze, at greening, and when grain is filling. I spray two times, once for weeds, once when the wheat gets sick with that rust. I hire the tractor man for rotary tilling, 40 yuan the mu. My back can't do the plowing no more. Wheat gives me 450 kg per mu in a good year, less when it's dry.

Corn goes straight in after wheat harvest, June. No tilling — just the seed drill behind the wheat cutter. I use hybrid seed, the one the dealer says everybody buys. Compound fertilizer at planting, one bag per mu. Then when the corn is knee-high I topdress with urea, about half a bag per mu. Total nitrogen maybe 20 kg. I water two times if the rain don't come. Spray twice for the corn borer. Corn gives me 500 kg per mu.

Cotton is more work but I know it. Plant in April after plowing. One bag compound at planting, then urea when it's flowering. I spray more — bollworms are the devil, five, six times. Irrigate three times from the well. Cotton gives me 230 kg seed cotton per mu.

I'd rather spend a little extra on fertilizer than see a thin harvest. Fertilizer is money wasted; a bad harvest is hunger.
